items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-23
items.q: Roy Evans, Sun Handy, Lee Collie, myself, Joe Robo Show. And that was all. No, Plectum. We called the guy Plectum. That'd be one of the greatest band you play around here.

ctx.x: Why he got off of that, I don't know. And that was the bad consistor. Roy Evans, Sun Handy, Lee Collie, myself, Joe Robo Show. And that was all. No, Plectum. We called the guy Plectum. That'd be one of the greatest band you play around here. I'll see his name, and I'll see if I can think his name now. I called him Plectum, because he's one of them Plectum guitars. Five-string guitars. Panties now. What is that little fellow man now? He turned out to be one of the greatest. He's in New York now. New York's 12-8.…
Yeah, well, did he play with Lee Collin's at the Astoria too? Yeah. The same banjo player? Yeah. Well, he had a couple of them there. He had Rene Hall and he had Rene Hall. Rene Hall. That's it.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: For two years, man, we did that, no day off.

ctx.x: Man, that, that guy would play until, uh, the man threw his hand up, then he'd go out. Uh, he'd go out and see what he'd go out and see what he'd go out and see what he'd go out. Sound didn't get out, knockin' off another, no. Well, we had a siftin' play. For two years, man, we did that, no day off. No Sunday or nothin', if you wanna get off something like that, he'd send somebody to inflation.
Who was this, uh, Lee and you and you said Sun Handy? Sun Handy, Johnny Handy.
All right. Saxophone player. You've met him?
